title: tshark decode workflows
intro: Work from the module directory. Treat the **`.tsv`** files (**`http_tls_fields.tsv`**, **`dns_fields.tsv`**, **`mixed_addr.tsv`**) as tab-separated tables.

questions.prompt: From **`http_tls_fields.tsv`**, print **every data line** (skip header) where **`tcp_dstport`** is **`443`**. Print the **full** line each time.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Filter TSV rows on the destination port column.

questions.prompt: From **`http_tls_fields.tsv`**, list **`ip_src`** for rows where **`tcp_dstport`** is **`80`**. **Unique**, **sorted** ascending, one IP per line.
In **one line** (no shell command), give a Wireshark **display filter** for **TCP segments whose destination port is 443** using **`tcp.dstport==443`**.
From **`dns_fields.tsv`**, print **`dns_qry_name`** only for rows where that name **contains** **`cdn`** (case-sensitive), **file order**.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Substring filter on the query-name column.

questions.prompt: How many rows in **`dns_fields.tsv`** have **`combo`** containing **`response`**? Print **only** the integer.

From **`http_tls_fields.tsv`**, for data rows where **`http_method`** is exactly **`GET`**, print **`frame_num`:`ip_src`:`http_host`** (no spaces around colons), **one per match**, sorted by **`frame_num`** numeric ascending.
From **`mixed_addr.tsv`**, print **full data lines** (not the header) where **`ip_dst`** contains **`:`** (IPv6 textual heuristic).
questions.solutionMarkdown: Filter non-header rows whose destination has a colon.

questions.prompt: In **one sentence**, how does a **capture filter** (BPF, **`tcpdump`** while sniffing) differ from a **display filter** (**`tshark -Y`** on a read trace)?
questions.expectedOutput: Capture filters are BPF expressions evaluated while packets are collected (limited primitives, no per-field Wireshark dissector tree), whereas display filters are Wireshark expressions applied after capture to already-decoded frames and their fields (what tshark -Y uses).

questions.prompt: From **`http_tls_fields.tsv`**, which **`ip_src`** appears on the **largest** number of rows (all ports)? Tie-break: lexicographically smallest IP. Print **only** that IP.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Count rows per **`ip_src`**; pick the max count.

questions.prompt: Name the three **`tshark`** flags for: **(a)** read packets from a file, **(b)** display filter, **(c)** **`-T fields`** style output. Short forms fine.
questions.expectedOutput: (a) -r (read capture file). (b) -Y (display filter). (c) -T fields (tabular field output; typically with repeated -e).

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes

- Run **`tshark`** on a file with **`-r`**, narrow with **`-Y`** **display filters**, and project columns with **`-T fields`** and **`-e`**.
- Relate **Wireshark display filter** syntax to the **field names** you export (e.g. **`ip.src`**, **`tcp.dstport`**, **`dns.qry.name`**).
- Post-process **tab-separated** **`tshark`** output using **`awk`** / **`sort`** like any other TSV.
- State the difference between **BPF capture filters** and **display filters**.

## Scope

**In scope:** read-only decode, batch extraction, small filters. **Out of scope:** full TLS decryption setup, **Lua** dissectors, **`-X`** extcap plugins.

## Concept outline

1. **Invocation** — **`tshark -r file.pcap`**, **`-n`** / **`-N`** name resolution toggles, **`-c`** frame cap.
2. **Display filters** — same language as Wireshark GUI; examples **`tcp.dstport==443`**, **`dns.qry.name contains "cdn"`**, **`ip.version == 6`**.
3. **`-T fields`** — repeated **`-e`** builds columns; **`-E separator=\t`**, **`-E header=y`**, **`-E occurrence=f`** for multi-value fields.
4. **Performance** — narrow **`-Y`** early; avoid giant **`-e`** lists until needed; consider **`tshark -G fields`** for discovery.
5. **Platform** — Wireshark **CLI** builds differ slightly by packaging; field names track the upstream **Wireshark** release.

## Tooling and alternatives

| Task | Primary | Alternatives |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Decode PCAP to text | `tshark` | Wireshark GUI, **`capinfos`**, **`editcap`** for slicing |
| Regex on payloads | `tshark -Y` + `frame contains` | **`ngrep`**, **`tcpdump -A`** quick ASCII |
| Huge batch stats | `tshark` + `awk` / DuckDB | **Brim** / **Zed**, **Moloch**/**Arkime** |
